content.title: Philadelphia Phillies Opening Day roster about set. Who made 2026 team?
content.text: March 23, 2026Updated March 24, 2026, 1:14 p.m. ETOpening Day 2026 is nearly here and that means MLB rosters are just about set.While there weren't many positions up for grabs heading into spring training, the Philadelphia Phillies did have a number of changes with nearly a dozen different players likely to make the roster out of Clearwater.Newcomers this year include former Texas Ranger Adolis Garcia, who takes over in right fielder for Nick Castellanos after his release in February.Two rookies also made the roster, with Justin Crawford winning the centerfield job and Andrew Painter set as the team's fifth starter.Fresh off Team USA's 3-2 World Baseball Classic final loss to Venezuela, Phillies stars Bryce Harper and Kyle Schwarber return to the club with the hopes of leading Philly back to the postseason for a fifth straight year.While veteran starter Zack Wheeler is still on the mend following thoracic outlet decompression surgery, and Aaron Nola is looking to rebound from a subpar 2025, lefties Cristopher Sánchez and Jesús Luzardo are back at the top of the rotation after signing contract extensions this offseason.The Phillies will also be led by veterans such as shortstop Trea Turner, outfielder Brandon Marsh, second baseman Bryson Stott and catcher J.T. Realmuto, who returns after re-signing in the offseason.However, the Phils will be without outfielder Johan Rojas, who was suspended by MLB for the first 80 games after a positive test for the performance-enhancing substance Boldenone.While the team hasn't officially announced its Opening Day roster, here's a look at how things are likely to shake out to start the season as the Phils look to avenge last season's heartbreaking National League Divisional Series loss to the Los Angeles Dodgers.Phillies projected roster for 2026 seasonCatchersJ.T. RealmutoRafael MarchanInfieldersBryce HarperBryson StottTrea TurnerAlec BohmEdmundo SosaDylan MooreOutfieldersBrandon MarshJustin CrawfordAdolis GarciaOtto KempDesignated hitterKyle SchwarberStarting rotationCristopher SanchezAaron NolaJesus LuzardoTaijuan WalkerAndrew Painter* Zack Wheeler to begin season on IL.BullpenJhoan DuranJose AlvaradoBrad KellerTanner BanksJonathan BowlanKyle BackhusZach PopTim Mayza * Orion Kerkering and Max Lazar to begin season on IL.Who didn't make the Phillies roster?While the majority of the Phillies roster was set coming into camp, there were a number of battles for the bench and bullpen.The most well-known player not to make the club is longtime catcher Garrett Stubbs, who got beat out for the backup job by Marchan. Stubbs could be traded or might be sent down like he was last season following spring training.Here are some players who didn't make the cut:Garrett Stubbs, CBryan De La Cruz, OF (Reassigned to minor league camp)Zach McCambley, RHP (Rule-5 pick returned to Miami Marlins)Chase Shugart, RHP (Optioned to Lehigh Valley IronPigs)Seth Johnson, RHP (Optioned to Lehigh Valley IronPigs)Nolan Hoffman, RHP (Optioned to Lehigh Valley IronPigs)Pedro León, OF (Optioned to Lehigh Valley IronPigs)Alan Range, RHP (Optioned to Lehigh Valley IronPigs)Alex McFarlane, RHP (Optioned to Reading Fightin Phils)Moisés Chace, RHP (Optioned to Lehigh Valley IronPigs)Yoniel Curet, RHP (Optioned to Lehigh Valley IronPigs)Jean Cabrera, RHP (Optioned to Lehigh Valley IronPigs)Gabriel Rincones Jr., OF (Optioned to Lehigh Valley IronPigs)Phillies projected lineup for 2026 seasonHere's a projected Phillies lineup, according to Fangraphs:Trea Turner, SSKyle Schwarber, DHBryce Harper, 1BAlec Bohm, 3BBrandon Marsh, LFAdolis Garcia, RFBryson Stott, 2BJ.T. Realmuto, CJustin Crawford, CFWho is starting Opening Day for Phillies?With Wheeler likely out until May, 2025 NL Cy Young runner up Sanchez will take the mound for his first Opening Day start of his career.Here are the last 10 Phillies Opening Day starters:2025: Zack Wheeler2024: Zack Wheeler2023: Aaron Nola2022: Aaron Nola2021: Aaron Nola2020: Aaron Nola2019: Aaron Nola2018: Aaron Nola2017: Jeremy Hellickson2016: Jeremy HellicksonWho has the most Opening Day starts for Phillies?According to Baseball Reference, here's a look at which pitchers have the most Opening Day starts in Phillies history:Steve Carlton: 14 (10 consecutive)Robin Roberts: 12 (all consecutive)Aaron Nola: 6 (all consecutive)Chris Short: 6 (4 consecutive)Grover Alexander: 5 (4 consecutive)Curt Schilling: 5 (3 consecutive)Roy Halladay: 3 (all consecutive)Brett Myers: 3 (all consecutive)Terry Mulholland: 3 (all consecutive)Hal Carlson: 3 (all consecutive)Jimmy Ring: 3As far as position players, here's the most Opening Day starts for any regular as a Phillie:Mike Schmidt: 16 (all consecutive)Jimmy Rollins: 14 (all consecutive)Larry Bowa: 12 (all consecutive)Mike Lieberthal: 10 (all consecutive)Roy Thomas: 10 (all consecutive)Ryan Howard: 10 (6 consecutive)Richie Ashburn: 10 (6 consecutive)Granny Hamner: 10 (5 consecutive)Greg Luzinski: 9 (all consecutive)Johnny Callison: 9 (all consecutive)Willie Jones: 9 (all consecutive)Cy Williams: 9 (all consecutive)Fred Luderus: 9 (all consecutive)Mickey Doolin: 9 (all consecutive)Del Ennis: 9 (8 consecutive)Pat Burrell: 8 (all consecutive)Von Hayes: 8 (all consecutive)Sherry Magee: 8 (7 consecutive)Bobby Abreu: 8 (6 consecutive)Carlos Ruiz: 8 (5 consecutive)Chase Utley: 8 (5 consecutive)Chuck Klein: 8 (5 consecutive)John Titus: 8 (4 consecutive twice)Red Dooin: 8 (3 consecutive twice)J.T. Realmuto: 7 (all consecutive)Darren Daulton: 7 (all consecutive)Gary Maddox: 7 (all consecutive)Jimmie Wilson: 7 (4 consecutive)* Opening Day games dating back to 1898.When is Phillies Opening Day 2026?The Phillies open the season at 4:15 p.m. on March 26 against the Texas Rangers at Citizens Bank Park.This is the second time the Phillies have faced the Rangers on Opening Day. In 2023, they lost to the Rangers, 11-7, at Globe Life Park in Arlington, Texas.How can I get Phillies single-game tickets?The Phillies are selling tickets to all 81 home games on the team's website.You can also get tickets by using the button below:Get Phillies tickets at Citizens Bank ParkHow to stream Phillies games on PHILLIES.TVLast year, Major League Baseball and the NBC Regional Sports Networks announced a partnership to stream games direct-to-customers for the Phillies through the MLB App. The games are streamed on PHILLIES.TV.PHILLIES.TV will broadcast games and pregame and postgame shows during the regular season in the Phillies' home television market. The games will also be available on demand.To get PHILLIES.TV you can sign up here.Along with MLB.TV, certain Phillies games may be streamed on Netflix, Peacock and Apple TV+.Watch MLB games on PeacockWhat channels are Phillies games on?Phillies games are on NBC Sports Philadelphia, NBC 10 and NBC Sports Philadelphia+. National games are broadcast FOX, FS1, TBS, ESPN/ABC and MLB Network.The radio broadcast will be on 94WIP and WDEL 101.7 FM/1150 AM.Phillies scheduleThe Phillies will have a number of good series at Citizens Bank Park this year, but the homestand after the All-Star break in July is epic. The Phillies host the New York Mets for three games, followed by the Los Angeles Dodgers for three games and finally the New York Yankees for three games. For the full 2026 schedule, check the Phillies website.Here's a look at some key dates and series in Philadelphia during the 2026 season.Opening Day: March 26 vs. Texas RangersNew York Mets: June 18-20 and July 17-19All-Star Game in Philadelphia: July 14New York Yankees: July 24-26Atlanta Braves: April 17-19 and Sept. 4-7Pittsburgh Pirates: June 29-July 2Los Angeles Dodgers: July 20-22Field of Dreams games vs. Minnesota: Aug. 13 in Dyersville, IowaSt. Louis Cardinals: Aug. 21-23
